title: Review academic readability with explicit meaning-preserving calibration
instruction: C1/C2: Review academic readability as well as grammatical correctness. A grammatical sentence can merit a STYLE proposal when a more direct subject/action, an explicit parallel or a named quantity has a concrete reader benefit. Restore an omitted subject or verb when it prevents misreading or materially eases a difficult parallel; keep immediately recoverable gapping. Give the complete replacement and its benefit; retain clear prose and legitimate technical agency. C8: Preserve whether a comparison states an inequality or a dependency; do not turn one into the other. A4: Keep rank or ratio descriptions distinct from accuracy against ground truth, including the subset actually labelled in a caption. Reread combined replacements for syntax and scientific meaning.
scope: Academic editing of existing English scientific prose, especially Methods definitions and Results/caption explanations. No edit quota, blanket word/voice ban, forced expansion of clear ellipsis or new journal house style.
rationale: Private expert-edit comparisons revealed useful readability changes to grammatical prose that a conservative review could miss. Existing C1/C2, C8 and A4 provide the principles; this proposal adds a positive editing criterion and worked fix/keep cases instead of new rule IDs or a synonym dictionary.

sources.reference: Private language-expert edit comparisons; source passages, identities and complete reviews are withheld. Reader benefits and safeguards are the contributor's interpretations.
All examples and counterexamples in this proposal are newly constructed illustrations; they are not quotations from the private manuscripts.

examples.original: In the second group, where records are incomplete, there are six sites.
examples.proposed: The second group, where records are incomplete, includes six sites.
examples.context: Synthetic group-size result whose long opening separates the group from its count.
examples.reason: Use the group as a direct subject while preserving six and the incomplete-record condition. The original is grammatical; the improvement is STYLE.

examples.original: Source A records the entrance, source B the platform on the other side of the station.
examples.proposed: Source A records the entrance; source B records the platform on the other side of the station.
examples.context: Synthetic source comparison where the long parallel is difficult to recover.
examples.reason: Repeat the short verb to make both source/action relations explicit; do not expand every clear elliptical clause.

examples.original: The larger the two regions, the closer their centres.
examples.proposed: The distance between the centres is less than the mean radius of the two regions.
examples.context: Synthetic notes establish only d < (r1+r2)/2, with no dependency between changes in d and changes in r.
examples.reason: Express the supplied inequality instead of an unsupported covariation claim.

examples.original: The underestimating and overestimating sites are labelled.
examples.proposed: The sites with the lowest and highest ratios are labelled.
examples.context: Synthetic figure labels selected extreme ratios between two estimates; neither estimate is established as ground truth.
examples.reason: Preserve rank and the selected subset without adding an accuracy criterion.

counterexamples.context: A short clear introduction to a supplied two-item list.
counterexamples.why_keep: A direct existential introduction is useful; there is no blanket ban on there are.

counterexamples.context: The model and target quantity are already defined.
counterexamples.why_keep: Conventional scientific agency is clear; a more formal synonym adds no reader benefit.

counterexamples.text: The higher the applied voltage, the larger the measured current.
counterexamples.context: A synthetic experiment establishes this dependency over the stated range.
counterexamples.why_keep: The comparative correlative correctly expresses the supplied relation.

counterexamples.text: The model underestimates travel time relative to the observed traces.
counterexamples.context: Observed traces are the supplied justified reference in this synthetic test.
counterexamples.why_keep: The baseline and meaning of underestimation are explicit; accuracy language is appropriate.

comparisons.reason: Adds a concrete reader-benefit criterion for grammatical but difficult academic prose and positive calibration.
Adds inequality-versus-dependency calibration within the existing comparison rule.
Adds caption rank-versus-truth and labelled-subset calibration.
Recognise a materially difficult parallel as a reason to restore a verb while retaining immediately recoverable gapping.
Finite clauses already help overloaded constructions; no ban on absolute constructions is added.
Names must resolve the correct referent; clear pronouns remain valid.
Negation, quantifiers and claim strength already require preservation.
Direct action wording extends the existing nominalisation guidance without banning technical nouns.
Baseline and comparison direction safeguards remain unchanged.
Two source estimates do not establish ground truth; caption example makes that guard observable.
The equation defines the compared quantity and scale; no new scientific-validation claim.
Labels need to describe the displayed metric and subset.

privacy.note: Inspected payload contains only generalised provenance and synthetic examples. No manuscript excerpts, names, expert comments, source PDFs/DOCX, local settings or private paths. Public PR submission authorised by the user on 2026-10-30.
